The `_helpers.ftl` template in every advanced theme defines FreeMarker macros and functions that the page templates share. Page templates call a macro with the `helpers` prefix, such as `[@helpers.main]`. When you edit a macro in `_helpers.ftl`, the change applies to every page that calls the macro.

This page lists the macros and functions in the default theme. Macro names that start with an underscore, such as `_input_text`, are internal to other macros and aren't listed. The default `_helpers.ftl` template is the full reference for every macro. To view the template, edit a theme in the Admin UI and open the **Helpers** template.

## How Macros Work

Most layout macros wrap content with `[#nested/]`. FreeMarker inserts the content between a macro's opening and closing tags at the `[#nested/]` element. For example, the `html` macro has the following definition:

```html title="HTML helper"
[#macro html]
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  [#nested/]
</html>
[/#macro]
```

A page template calls the macro like this:

```html title="Example usage of HTML macro"
[@helpers.html]
<body>
Hello world!
</body>
[/@helpers.html]
```

The page then renders the following HTML:

```html title="Example result"
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<body>
Hello world!
</body>
</html>
```

## Page Layout

The following macros render the structure of each page:

* `html` renders the `<html>` element.
* `head` renders the `<head>` element, including the `<title>`, CSS, JavaScript, and meta tags. The `head` macro loads Prime.js, which the social login and CAPTCHA scripts need. When you replace the `head` macro, keep the Prime.js `<script>` tag.
* `body` renders the `<body>` element.
* `header` renders the page header. On the account pages, the header includes a logout link.
* `main` renders the main content panel of the hosted login pages, with the logo, the page title, alerts, and the locale selector.
* `footer` renders the footer of each page, including the "Powered by FusionAuth" link.
* `accountMain` renders the main content area of the self-service account pages, with alerts and an `accountFooter`.
* `accountFooter` renders the locale selector and the action links at the bottom of an account page. `accountMain` calls `accountFooter`.
* `accountPanel` renders a panel on the account pages with the user's profile image and name, plus an edit link when `showEdit` is true.
* `accountPanelFull` renders a full-width panel with an optional title on the account pages.
* `localeSelector` renders a drop-down that switches the page between English and the theme's additional locales.
* `orSeparator` renders a horizontal divider with the localized word "or".
* `progressBar` renders an animated bar that fills over `durationSeconds` seconds. The logout pages use `progressBar`.
* `codeBox` renders preformatted text, such as a user's recovery codes.

### accountMain Parameters

<APIBlock>
  <APIField name="actionURL" type="String or Array" optional>
    The URL of the link in the footer. Pass an array to render several links. FusionAuth adds `client_id`, `tenantId`, and `redirect_uri` to each URL when the URL doesn't already contain them.
  </APIField>
  <APIField name="actionText" type="String or Array" optional defaults="Go back">
    The text of the link in the footer. When **`actionURL`** is an array, pass an array of the same length.
  </APIField>
  <APIField name="actionDirection" type="String" optional defaults="back">
    The arrow on the footer link. The value `back` puts a left arrow before the text. Any other value puts a right arrow after the text.
  </APIField>
  <APIField name="wide" type="Boolean" optional defaults="false">
    When true, the content area uses a wider maximum width.
  </APIField>
</APIBlock>

The `rowClass` and `colClass` parameters remain for compatibility with older themes. The default theme doesn't use them.

## Alerts and Errors

The `main` and `accountMain` macros call the following alert macros, so most pages don't need to call them directly:

* `printErrorAlerts` renders an `alert` for each message in the `errorMessages` template variable.
* `printInfoAlerts` renders an `alert` for each message in the `infoMessages` template variable.
* `alert` renders one error or info message. Call `alert` directly to show a message anywhere on a page.
* `errors` renders the field errors for one form field. The form field macros call `errors`. Call `errors` yourself only when you write your own form field markup.

### alert Parameters

<APIBlock>
  <APIField name="message" type="String" required>
    The message to display.
  </APIField>
  <APIField name="type" type="String" required>
    The alert style. The value `error` renders an error alert. Any other value renders an info alert.
  </APIField>
  <APIField name="icon" type="String" required>
    The Font Awesome icon name, such as `exclamation-circle` or `info-circle`.
  </APIField>
  <APIField name="includeDismissButton" type="Boolean" optional defaults="true">
    When true, the alert includes a button that closes the alert.
  </APIField>
</APIBlock>

## Forms

The following macros render forms and form fields. Each field macro renders a label, the field, and any errors for the field:

* `structuredForm` renders a `<form>` with one section for fields and one for buttons. The macro calls the nested content twice, first with `"formFields"` and then with `"buttons"`, so the nested content checks the section name. For an example, see the `oauth2/authorize.ftl` template.
* `hidden` renders a hidden input. When you don't pass a `value`, the macro reads the value of the request parameter with the same name.
* `oauthHiddenFields` renders the hidden inputs that carry the OAuth request through a form submit, such as `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `state`, and `scope`. Every form in the OAuth workflow calls `oauthHiddenFields`.
* `input` renders a text, password, date, number, or checkbox input. A password input includes a button that shows the password, unless you set `canShowPassword` to false.
* `select` renders a drop-down from the `options` list. For the `user.timezone` and `registration.timezone` fields, the macro lists the time zones instead.
* `textarea` renders a multi-line text field.
* `customField` renders a custom form field. The macro picks the field macro from the field's control type.
* `passwordField` renders the password fields on the account edit page.
* `passwordRules` renders the tenant's password requirements as a list. Pass the `passwordValidationRules` template variable.
* `scopeConsentField` renders the field for a requested OAuth scope on the OAuth consent prompt page. The macro picks the field type from the scope's consent mode, and uses the `resolveScopeMessaging` function for the text.
* `cimdClientDetails` <AvailableSince since="1.70.0"/> renders the name, host, `client_uri`, requested resource host, and redirect host of a [CIMD client](/docs/authentication/oauth/client-registration#client-id-metadata-documents) on the OAuth consent prompt page. The macro also warns the user when the redirect host is a loopback address. The default theme passes the `cimdClientName`, `cimdClientUri`, `cimdClientHost`, `cimdRedirectHost`, `cimdRedirectIsLoopback`, and `cimdResourceHost` template variables. The macro renders nothing when `clientHost` is empty, so other clients see no change.
* `required_checkbox_icon` renders a checked, disabled checkbox. `scopeConsentField` uses the icon for required scopes.
* `cssTooltip` renders a tooltip that appears on hover or focus. Pass the text as `text`, or pass a message key as `key`.

The following macros render the custom fields of an [advanced registration form](/docs/users/register/advanced-registration-forms). Each macro takes a `field` parameter, which only the registration and account edit pages provide. `customField` calls these macros, so you rarely call them directly:

* `checkbox` renders one checkbox.
* `checkbox_list` renders a checkbox for each value in `options`.
* `radio_list` renders a radio button for each value in `options`.
* `locale_select` renders a drop-down of every locale FusionAuth supports. The drop-down allows one selection.

### customField Parameters

<APIBlock>
  <APIField name="field" type="Object" required>
    The form field to render, from the form's field list.
  </APIField>
  <APIField name="key" type="String" required>
    The name of the input, such as `user.firstName`.
  </APIField>
  <APIField name="autofocus" type="Boolean" optional defaults="false">
    When true, the browser focuses the field when the page loads.
  </APIField>
  <APIField name="label" type="String" optional>
    The field label.
  </APIField>
  <APIField name="placeholder" type="String" optional>
    The message key for the placeholder text.
  </APIField>
  <APIField name="leftAddon" type="String" optional defaults="true">
    When `true`, the field shows the icon from the field's **`data.leftAddon`** value, or an info icon when the field has no value. Any other value hides the icon.
  </APIField>
</APIBlock>

### passwordField Parameters

<APIBlock>
  <APIField name="field" type="Object" required>
    The password form field.
  </APIField>
  <APIField name="showCurrentPasswordField" type="Boolean" optional defaults="false">
    When true, the macro adds a current password field. Pass true when the application requires the current password to change a password.
  </APIField>
</APIBlock>

The macro renders a toggle that shows the password fields. When the field's **`confirm`** value is true, the macro adds a confirm password field. After a password error, the macro also renders `passwordRules`.

## Buttons and Links

The following macros render buttons and links:

* `button` renders a submit button. The `style` parameter accepts `primary`, `delete`, or any other value for a plain button.
* `buttonLink` renders a link styled as a button.
* `linkButton` renders a button styled as a link.
* `link` renders a link that keeps the current OAuth request parameters, so the user stays in the same OAuth workflow. For example, the login page uses `link` for the forgot password link.
* `logoutLink` renders a link to `/oauth2/logout`. After logout, FusionAuth sends the user to `redirectURI` with the current OAuth request parameters.

### link and logoutLink Parameters

<APIBlock>
  <APIField name="url" type="String" required>
    `link` only. The path of the link, such as `/password/forgot`.
  </APIField>
  <APIField name="redirectURI" type="String" required>
    `logoutLink` only. The URL to send the user to after logout.
  </APIField>
  <APIField name="extraParameters" type="String" optional>
    Query parameters to add to the end of the URL. Start the value with `&`, such as `&showPasswordField=false`.
  </APIField>
</APIBlock>

Both macros use the nested content as the link text:

```html title="Example usage of the link macro"
[@helpers.link url="${request.contextPath}/password/forgot"]${theme.message('forgot-your-password')}[/@helpers.link]
```

## Social Login

The `_helpers.ftl` template renders the buttons for the [[social login]] and other identity providers configured for an application. The hosted login page and the registration page (`/oauth2/register`, available since FusionAuth `1.28.0`) call the following macros:

```html title="Social login code"
[@helpers.head]
  [@helpers.alternativeLoginsScript clientId=application.id identityProviders=identityProviders/]
  ...
[/@helpers.head]

[@helpers.body]
  ...
  [@helpers.alternativeLogins clientId=application.id identityProviders=identityProviders passwordlessEnabled=passwordlessEnabled bootstrapWebauthnEnabled=bootstrapWebauthnEnabled idpRedirectState=idpRedirectState federatedCSRFToken=federatedCSRFToken/]
[/@helpers.body]
```

`alternativeLoginsScript` adds the JavaScript for the configured identity providers to the `<head>` element. Without that JavaScript, the login buttons don't work.

`alternativeLogins` renders a button for each configured identity provider. The macro also renders the magic link button when passwordless login is on, and the passkey button when **`bootstrapWebauthnEnabled`** is true.

`alternativeLogins` calls a button macro for each identity provider type:

* `appleButton` for Apple.
* `epicButton` for Epic Games.
* `facebookButton` for Facebook.
* `googleButton` for Google, when Google uses the `UseRedirect` login method.
* `googleGsiButton` for Google, when Google uses the Google Identity Services API.
* `linkedInButton` for LinkedIn.
* `nintendoButton` for Nintendo.
* `openIDConnectButton` for OpenID Connect.
* `samlv2Button` for SAML v2.
* `sonypsnButton` for Sony PlayStation Network.
* `steamButton` for Steam.
* `twitchButton` for Twitch.
* `twitterButton` for Twitter.
* `xboxButton` for Xbox.

Each button macro except `googleGsiButton` calls `idpButton`. `idpButton` renders the `<button>` element, and each provider macro passes in the provider's icon as nested content. To change the icon or text of one provider's button, edit that provider's macro.

### Use Your Own Social Login Buttons

To replace the default buttons with your own markup, remove the `[@helpers.alternativeLogins]` call and write the buttons yourself. Keep the `alternativeLoginsScript` call in the `<head>` element. The identity provider JavaScript finds your buttons by class and data attributes, so each button needs the following:

* Wrap the buttons in an element with `id="login-button-container"` and `data-federated-csrf="${federatedCSRFToken}"`. The identity provider JavaScript reads the CSRF token from this element.
* Give each button the `login-button` class and a `data-identity-provider-id` attribute set to the identity provider's Id.
* For a provider that logs in with a redirect, add `data-login-method="UseRedirect"`. Epic Games, LinkedIn, Nintendo, OpenID Connect, SAML v2, Sony PlayStation Network, Steam, Twitch, and Xbox always log in with a redirect. Google and Facebook log in with a redirect when the identity provider's login method is `UseRedirect`.
* For Apple, add the `apple` class. For Facebook and Twitter without a redirect, add the `facebook` or `twitter` class. These buttons also need the data attributes that the `appleButton`, `facebookButton`, and `twitterButton` macros render, such as `data-scope`.

The form on the page must include a `client_id` input. The `oauthHiddenFields` macro adds one.

The following example renders a button for an OpenID Connect identity provider:

```html title="Custom OpenID Connect login button"
<div id="login-button-container" data-federated-csrf="${federatedCSRFToken}">
  [#list identityProviders["OpenIDConnect"]![] as identityProvider]
    <button class="login-button openidconnect"
            data-identity-provider-id="${identityProvider.id}"
            data-login-method="UseRedirect">
      ${identityProvider.lookupButtonText(application.id)}
    </button>
  [/#list]
</div>
```

The Google Identity Services button comes from Google's own JavaScript, so the requirements above don't apply to that button. To change that button, edit the `googleGsiButton` macro. For the available attributes, see the [Google Identity Services HTML reference](https://developers.google.com/identity/gsi/web/reference/html-reference).

## CAPTCHA

The `_helpers.ftl` template provides macros that add [CAPTCHA challenges](/docs/concepts/types/tenants#captcha-settings) to a page. A page that shows a CAPTCHA calls both macros:

* `captchaScripts` adds the CAPTCHA provider's JavaScript. Call `captchaScripts` inside the `head` macro.
* `captchaBadge` renders the CAPTCHA widget or badge, plus any CAPTCHA error. Call `captchaBadge` inside the form.

For more information on the template variables, see [Template Variables](/docs/theme/advanced-themes/template-variables).

### Parameters

Both macros take the following parameters:

<APIBlock>
  <APIField name="captchaMethod" type="String" required>
    The type of CAPTCHA to use. The default theme passes the `tenant.captchaConfiguration.captchaMethod` template variable. The valid values are:

    <RecaptchaValues />
  </APIField>
  <APIField name="showCaptcha" type="Boolean" required>
    When true, the macro renders the CAPTCHA. When false, the macro renders nothing. The default theme passes the `showCaptcha` template variable.
  </APIField>
  <APIField name="siteKey" type="String" optional>
    The site key for the CAPTCHA. The default theme passes the `tenant.captchaConfiguration.siteKey` template variable. When **`captchaMethod`** is `GoogleRecaptchaV3`, the CAPTCHA requires a site key.
  </APIField>
</APIBlock>

### Invisible reCAPTCHA

To challenge a form submit without a checkbox on the form, use an [invisible reCAPTCHA](https://developers.google.com/recaptcha/docs/invisible). Add the `data-size` and `data-callback` attributes to the element with the `g-recaptcha` class in the `captchaBadge` macro. In FusionAuth `1.46.0` and later, the default template includes these attributes in a comment.

```html title="Invisible tag"
[#if captchaMethod == "GoogleRecaptchaV2"]
      <div class="g-recaptcha" data-sitekey="${siteKey!''}"
        data-size="invisible"
        data-callback="reCaptchaV2InvisibleCallback"
      ></div>
 ...
```

<Aside type="note">
Before FusionAuth `1.46.0`, the form submit JavaScript also needs an update to handle an invisible reCAPTCHA. For more information, see [the 1.46.0 release notes](/docs/release-notes#version-1-46-0).
</Aside>

## Functions

The `_helpers.ftl` template also defines the following FreeMarker functions. Call a function inside an expression, such as `${helpers.display(user, "email")}`:

* `display` returns the value of a property on an object, such as `display(user, "name")`. The function formats numbers with thousands separators. When the property is empty, the function returns the `default` argument, which defaults to an en dash.
* `resolveScopeMessaging` returns the consent message or detail for an OAuth scope. The function checks for an application-specific message, then a tenant-specific message, then a general message, then returns the `default` argument.
* `addDataAttributes` turns a map into HTML `data-` attributes. `structuredForm` uses `addDataAttributes` for its `dataAttributes` parameter.

The `defaultIfNull` macro renders `text`, or `default` when `text` is missing.
